A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ScaleEdit work, with 16 readable pages including supplementary sections A–I. Text and rendered pages 2–16 are identical; page 1 has only a website addition, formatting adjustments, and an updated arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-editing experiments, including synthetic-image comparisons in Table 1, ablations in Tables 2–3, and real-image evaluation in Table 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, qualitative editing results, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The patch-wise procedure, learned detail transfer, synchronization, and Stable Diffusion/FLUX adaptations are unchanged in Section 4 and supplementary sections A–C.

E1.justification: Both retain the same synthetic editing tasks, 1K/2K evaluations, 8K demonstration, and supplementary real-image 1K evaluation. No dataset, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the same comparators: DiT-SR, DiT4SR, PiSA-SR, and TSD-SR. Comparator participation in the qualitative comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including 400 pairs per synthetic editing scenario, 285 real-image pairs, 60-pair ablations, metrics, backbones, T=50, and the default tau=15.

E4.justification: The synchronization ablations, tau sensitivity study, transfer-module design comparisons, and supplementary qualitative analyses are identical in both versions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both present the same point estimates without reported repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All values in Tables 1–4, qualitative result images, and supplementary runtime and memory measurements are unchanged. No results are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Equations 1–27, including the optimization objective, synchronization formulation, and supplementary flow-based adaptation, are identical. No assumptions or mathematical reasoning change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about high-resolution editing, detail transfer, synchronization, and editing performance. The added website pointer changes no scientific claim.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and supplementary discussions remain identical, including computational trade-offs and limitations from pretrained models and artifacts inherited from low-resolution reference images.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-website hyperlink at the end of the abstract. Implementation and resource-use details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the website supplies code or data.

R1.justification: The same 63 references, related-work discussion, and research positioning are retained. The project-website addition is not a new cited research comparison.

P1.justification: v3 appends a project-website line to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific wording, terminology, section order, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The website addition reflows the abstract and slightly shifts first-page elements, including Figure 1. Figure content and captions remain unchanged; pages 2–16 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, and appendices are identical. The added project-website pointer offers a small navigation convenience, but the supplied PDFs establish no meaningful overall quality gain or loss beyond this and minor first-page formatting changes.
